proof.title: Results from real engagements
proof.case1Problem: Leads flooding in via WhatsApp, email, and DMs. Too few people to respond. Deals were slipping.
proof.case1Solution: We built an AI lead management system across WhatsApp, website, and email: automatic responses, contact capture, CRM updates, and calendar booking.
proof.case2Problem: Customers kept asking questions already answered on the website. Staff spent 15 hours/week on repetitive replies.
proof.case2Solution: We deployed a customer-ready FAQ assistant grounded on real company data, with escalation to humans, unknown-question logging, and a weekly improvement loop.
proof.case2Result: From 15 hrs/week to 1.5 hrs/week on repetitive questions

faq.title: Questions before you reach out
faq.a1: B2B services firms (typically 10-200 people) who've tried AI or are under pressure to start, and want measurable results instead of more experiments.
faq.a2: It depends on scope. Book a free call and we'll tell you within 15 minutes whether the Sprint is a fit and what it would cost for your situation.
faq.q3: What if we already tried AI and it didn't work?
faq.a3: That's most of our clients. Usually the missing piece is prioritization, workflow fit, adoption, or guardrails. The Sprint finds what blocked ROI and fixes the approach.
faq.a4: Whatever fits your situation. We're tool-agnostic by design. No vendor lock-in, no forced platform changes.
faq.q5: How fast can we see results?
faq.a5: Clarity in 2 weeks. A production pilot in 4-6 weeks after that. Measurement starts from day one.

problem.title: Why most AI initiatives stall
problem.reason1: No ranked priorities. Everything feels equally urgent.
problem.reason2: Pilots never reach production. The demo works, then sits.
problem.reason3: Teams don't trust the outputs. Adoption stays low.
problem.reason4: Nobody is measuring ROI. So nobody knows what's working.
problem.bridgeLine: The Sprint solves all four in two weeks.

faq.title: Sprint FAQ
faq.a1: No. You leave with real deliverables: a workflow map, ranked opportunities, an ROI model, a 90-day plan, and a build-ready pilot spec.
faq.q2: Do you build anything during the Sprint?
faq.a2: No. The Sprint is for clarity and prioritization. Building happens in the Pilot phase (4-6 weeks), if you choose to continue.
faq.q3: What if we already tried AI and it failed?
faq.a3: That's common and usually fixable. The Sprint finds what went wrong: missing prioritization, poor workflow fit, weak adoption, or no guardrails.
faq.q4: Do we need perfect data to start?
faq.a4: No. We start workflow-first and identify the minimum data you actually need. If data quality is the blocker, the Sprint makes that visible early.
faq.a5: Not the goal. We design human-in-the-loop by default. AI supports your team; it doesn't replace the relationships your clients value.
faq.a6: Two layers. First: time saved (the most defensible metric). Second: revenue uplift (conversion, cycle time) modeled conservatively and validated with your team.
